solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A little boy, Winchester's sixth former

parts.note: a little of something is some of it
Tim is a boy's name

indicators.note: sixth says to take the sixth letter of the word Winchester

parts.note: W-I-N-C-H-E: the sixth letter is E

explanation.surface: A small lad who was once in the sixth form at Winchester College, the public school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixth former' looks like a senior pupil, but 'sixth' picks a letter and 'former' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime as an adjective means one-time or erstwhile, as in 'the sometime mayor'.

clue.text: "Save our NHS", say hospital nurses to Chronicle

indicators.note: nurses means holds closely, so the hospital word holds the next one inside

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
a log is a chronicle or record

explanation.surface: A campaign rallying cry about the health service, as hospital nurses tell a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; the quoted cry is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign catchphrase is a slogan, and this one is a well-known example.

clue.text: An eccentric revolutionary, that Spanish primate

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: taken as A
a cam is an eccentric, an off-centre rotating part in machinery
que is Spanish for that

explanation.surface: An oddball rebel, that Spanish ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaque is a kind of monkey, such as the rhesus or Barbary ape.

clue.text: Pasta to follow: one fabricating popular starter for Italians

parts.note: to tag along is to follow
a liar is one who makes things up
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: starter for says to take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter is I

explanation.surface: Pasta to come next: a cook making a popular first course for Italian diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliarini is a thin ribbon pasta, a narrower relative of tagliatelle.

clue.text: After motorway, turned up sideroad on the way to work

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: turned means twisted around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaving the motorway and turning onto a side road on the commute to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers UP, SIDEROAD and ON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Modus operandi is Latin for a method of working, the way a job is done.

clue.text: Breeding ground cultivated to catch disease

indicators.note: to catch says the cultivated word takes the disease inside it

parts.note: ground that has been hoed has been cultivated
TB is the usual abbreviation for tuberculosis

explanation.surface: A tilled patch where some infection might be picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is literally a heated bed of soil for raising plants, and figuratively a place where something flourishes.

clue.text: Books containing pictures for everyone to remove

indicators.note: containing says the books letters hold the next letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, so U films are Us

explanation.surface: Volumes with illustrations to clear away for all to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to remove someone from a post, to expel or eject.

clue.text: Roast cut by ladies, perhaps, and a cake

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the roast word loses its last letter

parts.note: to roast is to bake
lav is short for lavatory, and the ladies is one

explanation.surface: A joint sliced up by some women, with a cake to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the ladies' is a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a sweet pastry made of filo layers, nuts and honey, served like a cake.

clue.text: Scales down, at the outset, original RAF fund

indicators.note: at the outset says to take the first letter of down

parts.note: its first letter is D

indicators.note: original means novel or inventive, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The scales of an original RAF fund are reduced from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandruff is flakes of dead skin from the scalp, which are scales.

clue.text: Malevolent creature might, if out of bounds

indicators.note: out of bounds says the word for might loses its outer limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: might means strength or force

explanation.surface: A monster that might strike if it strays beyond the permitted area.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcs are the brutish, evil goblin soldiers of Tolkien's fantasy fiction.

clue.text: Attack the rice wine, with days in November being dreary!

indicators.note: in says the days letter sits inside the attack phrase

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them
sake is the Japanese rice wine
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone drinking sake through a gloomy month of November and lamenting it.
explanation.walkthrough: To go for someone is British and American idiom for attacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: A godforsaken place is bleak and desolate, so dreary is a fair loose synonym.

clue.text: Such as Maggie Tulliver, oddly in love: a rarity!

parts.note: Maggie Tulliver, heroine of George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss, is one living in a mill

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A literary heroine strangely in love, which is a rare thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks as if it picks alternate letters, but it shuffles IN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something or someone extraordinary, a rare find.

clue.text: Gave in a hundred pounds to get hold of key drug

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: to get hold of says the pounds word grips the key and drug inside it

parts.note: a quid is slang for a pound sterling and serves as a plural too
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered a hundred pounds to obtain a vital drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept or agree reluctantly, which is to give in.

clue.text: Broadcast clip showing match

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: to pare is to clip or trim

explanation.surface: A televised excerpt showing highlights of a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a matched couple, and to pair things is to match them.

clue.text: Buttress with ends of segment touching, and no good, therefore

indicators.note: ends of says to take the first and last letters of segment

parts.note: its ends are S and T
re means about or concerning, so touching
then means therefore

explanation.surface: Supporting something with the edges of a segment touching, which is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress something is to support or reinforce it.

clue.text: Go to town three times, the last two prematurely

indicators.note: the final two letters of the word for three times arrive early, moving to the front

parts.note: triple means three times as much

explanation.surface: A trip into town made three times, with the last two trips happening too early.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for acting without restraint or doing something lavishly and with gusto.

clue.text: Tie that's displaced the first semi, indeed

parts.note: a tie is a knot; with its first letter pushed out it leaves the rest
semi- means half

explanation.surface: A tie that has knocked out a semi-final, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOT loses its K, the letter 'that's displaced the first'. 'Not half!' is British slang for an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic agreement, much like saying very much so.

clue.text: Climber's later course, kilometre from summit

definitions.note: read as 'Climber is', the 's being a link

parts.note: the sweet is a dessert, a course later in the meal

indicators.note: from says the kilometre letter is taken away from the summit word

parts.note: a peak is a summit
K is short for kilometre

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's later route, a kilometre from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a fragrant annual plant that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Carter's wife doomed!

definitions.note: read as 'Carter is', the 's being a link

parts.note: someone doomed is a goner

explanation.surface: The wife of a man called Carter has no hope left.
explanation.walkthrough: Carter looks like a surname; it is a carter, one who drives a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A carter and a wagoner both drive horse-drawn goods vehicles for a living.

clue.text: Suffers with effect of freefall here?

definitions.text: Suffers with effect of freefall here?

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity, what a body in freefall experiences
to suffer is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: Someone enduring the pull of gravity on the drop from a gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a hanging, where the condemned falls through the trapdoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows is the frame for hanging, where victims drop to their deaths.

clue.text: Fare reducing entails EU ministers backtracking

indicators.note: backtracking says the hidden letters are read backwards
reducing means cutting down, so the words that follow are cut down to a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A policy that cuts transport prices, involving European Union ministers making a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare reducing' looks like a phrase about cheaper tickets; Fare alone is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit, so a kind of food.

clue.text: The state in which old police chief's bearing left one

indicators.note: bearing means carrying in front, so the chief comes with the other letters leading

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Lavrentiy Beria was head of Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A country where a former police chief's demeanour leaves someone behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African country, so a nation or state.

clue.text: Part of snooker's scoring system given a makeover?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in snooker potting a red ball scores one point

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses split differently: RED ONE for the snooker score, REDONE for the refit.
explanation.definitionFit: A refurbished room has been redecorated, and a red ball is worth one point.

clue.text: Building extensions taken to extend much more than an inch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ell is a wing built at right angles to a main building

definitions.text: taken to extend much more than an inch
definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the proverb 'give him an inch and he'll take an ell', an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a person given a small concession grabs a far larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of an old unit of length and of an L-shaped annexe to a house.

clue.text: ie, being ill adapted?

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: That is, being unsuited for something because of sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, being ill adapted is a reason for not qualifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfit or unqualified for a role is not entitled to be chosen for it.

clue.text: Forbidding party game to be taken up

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means read upwards, so the game letters are reversed

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A party game that is banned from being adopted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like banning; here it is an adjective meaning stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A dour person is stern and severe, grim-faced and unwelcoming.

clue.text: Quietly getting shot of horse in one (in some way)?

definitions.text: Quietly getting shot of horse in one (in some way)?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: in some way says the letters before it are taken in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
H is slang for heroin, known as horse, then IN as written and I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Discreetly taking a picture of a racehorse at the decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and brackets hint that the whole clue also describes the answer: a close race judged from a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A close race result decided by a photograph of the runners crossing the line.

clue.text: Bounder deposing the king of the castle

indicators.note: deposing says the king is removed from the chess piece

parts.note: the rook is also called the castle in chess
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A cad who topples the reigning monarch in the children's game king of the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like an old word for a cad; it is something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo, short for kangaroo, moves by leaping, so it is literally a bounder.

clue.text: A magpie, for example, heard devouring small cuckoo

indicators.note: devouring says the sounded word swallows the small letter
heard says the word is taken as it sounds, written another way

parts.note: a magpie is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: A magpie heard eating a little cuckoo chick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' seems to be another bird with the magpie; it is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is informal for mad or ridiculous, which is what absurd means.

clue.text: At home, maybe take time away from flood

parts.note: in means at home
whimsically, to undate is to spend time away from someone, the opposite of a date; the dictionary also has it as removing a date

explanation.surface: Perhaps staying at home rather than going out, to escape some flooding.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, swamping land completely.
